notes:
What's new in Vekrun 0.7.4

• Ask for Stripe and get it working: a request like "add Stripe billing" or a project that already uses Stripe now sets up a local Stripe test server in the build machine. Live keys are refused; the setup proves itself by creating a test payment and a Checkout Session, and checks that a bad request is turned down. No Stripe account or real payment is ever involved.
• Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui, properly: ask for Tailwind (v4 or v3) or shadcn/ui on a Next.js, Laravel, Rails or Django project — or open one that already uses them — and Vekrun sets them up the way each framework officially does it. What your project already uses always wins; combinations that can't work (shadcn/ui on Tailwind v3, or without React) are explained instead of half-installed.
• Every proof now lists the recipes it used (for example "Node.js · Express · Stripe billing (test mode) 0.1.0"), and Environment → Toolchains shows the same line.
• Vekrun understands more existing projects: older Node, PHP, Ruby and Python projects, repositories that still point at git:// remotes, and Python packages that need build headers now set up correctly. On our test set of real-world projects, correct detection went from 43% to 81%.
• Projects with several parts — a backend/ and a frontend/, a server/ and a client/ — now get each part installed and tested in its own folder, instead of only the root.
• Official logos for Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Gemini and OpenRouter on the welcome screens and in Agents.
• The Board's ticket list now fills the window, and selecting several tickets no longer pushes the layout around.
• Under the hood: what Vekrun knows about each stack now lives in versioned recipe descriptions instead of code, so new stacks can be added without changing how existing projects are set up — every existing project sets up exactly as it did in 0.7.3.
